All Data In Your Environment Faddom does not send any information or data outside of the appliance itself. All the information is collected and stored on the Faddom server, inside your environment. Security Is In Your Hands As the Faddom appliance sits inside your own environment, all access and security rules are defined by yourselves. There is no need for Faddom staff or other third parties to have access. Faddom supports integration with Active Directory or LDAP to give credentials only to whoever needs access. It’s Read-Only Faddom does not and cannot make any changes to your environment. It shows you the environment and can highlight issues that you need to resolve. Application mapping is a visual, graphical representation of an organization’s software applications, infrastructure components, and their interconnecting dependencies. Application mapping is the process of identifying all the elements in a software ecosystem, while mapping the interactions and relationships between applications and infrastructure. An application map visualizes the devices applications in a network and how they are related. Application dependency mapping , or ADM, is a subset of application mapping that identifies which applications are dependent on what, in the context of your entire network. The goal is to help organizations understand the complex connections between their various software, hardware, and related systems. Application mapping helps organizations automate the discovery of virtual resources. It can provide administrators with an overview of key dependencies and give IT managers a clear picture of their environmental health and overall application performance. Application mapping can be done manually by examining code and system architecture, or using automated tools that scan the application and generate a visual representation. Application mapping or ADM tools create a topology map that identifies and maps out all the instances, communications channels, and applications in your IT ecosystem as well as the ports and services that are being used. The best solutions can also quickly and easily define VPCs, subnets, and security groups on cloud providers such as AWS, Azure, and GPS. When displayed on an intuitive map, you have a visual representation of your application dependencies that can be shared, examined, or used for planning and troubleshooting. This visualization can be used for business strategy, organizing by business context, and prioritizing critical alerts and information in real time. Cloud migrations are complex transitions that frequently lead to budget overruns, security vulnerabilities, and operational downtime if not properly executed. Key challenges include aligning legacy system compatibility, bridging internal skills gaps, and avoiding vendor lock-in with major hyperscalers. The most critical hurdles organizations face include: Limited visibility into existing infrastructure: Missing asset inventories make migration planning inaccurate. Incomplete application dependency mapping: Hidden dependencies increase the risk of outages during migration. Choosing the wrong migration strategy: A poor migration approach can increase costs and reduce cloud benefits. Unexpected cloud migration costs: Hidden infrastructure, licensing, and data transfer costs strain budgets. Data migration complexity: Large datasets require careful synchronization and validation. Security and privacy risks: Misconfigurations can expose sensitive data during and after migration. Regulatory and compliance requirements: Cloud deployments must meet industry and regional regulations. Application compatibility and modernization issues: Legacy applications may require significant redesign before migration. Performance and latency problems: Cloud architectures can introduce network and application delays. Business disruption and downtime: Poor planning can interrupt critical business operations.
